Trust model: the local user account and its writable files are inside pi's trust boundary; no sandbox and no permission system by design; prompt injection and malicious model output declared out of scope and unfixable; private reporting via security@earendil.com or a GitHub Security Advisory.

Windows source-run script: --no-env unsets 36 provider and cloud credential env vars, and the resolver path is converted to a file URL with [System.Uri].AbsoluteUri because --import takes a module specifier, not a path.

POSIX source-run script: the same --no-env credential stripping; the resolver path is converted via node pathToFileURL because raw paths containing # ? or % corrupt the specifier; ${ARGS[@]+...} keeps an empty argument list safe under set -u.

The hermetic test entry point: mktemp sandbox, env -i allowlist environment (HOME/TMP/XDG redirected, git prompt-hijacking disabled, AWS_EC2_METADATA_DISABLED, PI_NO_LOCAL_LLM, proxy CA passed through), and a guarded cleanup that refuses to delete an unverified directory and flips the exit status to 1.

Shared compiler contract: strict, erasableSyntaxOnly (no enum, parameter properties or namespace), verbatimModuleSyntax, allowImportingTsExtensions with rewriteRelativeImportExtensions, declaration plus maps and inline sources.
Root typecheck project: noEmit, NodeNext, and a paths map resolving every workspace specifier including subpaths to src/; include covers packages/*/src, packages/*/test and two example trees.
Shared Vitest base: workspaceSourcePaths maps every package specifier to its SOURCE index and the alias table derives from that map, so a test can never pass against a stale build.
